title: SSP-8 — Revised Model
summary: revise document lineage as a Working-owned set of Editorial children after immediate public cleanup on document Delete
content_html:
SSP-8 — Revised Model

Status And Purpose

SSP-8.2 is complete and stopped at its review gate before SSP-8.3. DPD-1 — Immediate Public Projection Cleanup On Document Delete is complete and parked, so the prerequisite is satisfied. SSP-8.2 replaced the interim nullable-state table with the strict Working-owned v3 table, migrated the reviewed data explicitly, and adapted the existing lineage-aware Copy path without starting Delete or revised Publish follow-through.

The earlier independently nullable Working, Editorial, and Published model was rejected after review exposed two simpler product facts:

  1. lineage exists to trace what happened to a current Working document in dotlineform/projects; and
  2. deleting editable canonical source must immediately remove its now-unmaintainable public projection rather than waiting for scope Publish.

SSP-8.0 — Superseded Independent-State Sanity Note and SSP-8.1 — Superseded Nullable-State Cutover Evidence are retained review history, not the current contract. SSP-8.2 replaced their interim v2 nullable-state table in one clean cut after DPD-1 established immediate public cleanup.

Working-Owned Lineage

The exact Working doc_id is the lineage key. Working is not a promotion state, carries no status, and needs no icon. SSP-8.2 removed the separate lineage_id because it duplicated the only identity that makes the record relevant.

One Working document may have zero, one, or several exact Editorial children in analysis/works. Every child exists only because the configured lineage-aware Copy created it. Directly created Working or Editorial documents do not acquire lineage from location, title, subject, public URL, or later publication.

The conceptual record is:

{
  "working_doc_id": "d-working",
  "editorials": [
    {
      "doc_id": "d-editorial",
      "created_at": "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ",
      "last_copied_at": "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ",
      "published_url": null
    }
  ]
}

The exact persisted envelope is docs_document_publication_lineage_v3 with required working_collection, editorial_collection, and records fields. Records sort by exact working_doc_id; Editorial children sort by exact doc_id. Both configured collection identities are stored once in the envelope, every record has at least one child, Working IDs are unique, and an Editorial ID belongs to only one Working record. There is no separate branch ID, nullable Working state, independent Published state, empty Working-only record, or v2 compatibility reader.

Action Rules

Copy

Copy looks up the exact Working doc_id:

  • no Editorial children means the ordinary choice is New;
  • one or more current Editorial children provide the exact New or Replace choices;
  • New creates a fresh Editorial document and child;
  • Replace selects one exact current Editorial doc_id, preserves its identity and publishable gate, and updates its copy evidence; and
  • Copy performs no comparison, diff, merge, automatic choice, or publication.

Publish

Scope-wide Publish remains the manually instigated positive promotion action. It sets or retains published_url for current publishable Editorial children and clears it only when an explicit publishable: false gate excludes that surviving child or its required public host. Editing content or setting publishable: false leaves the existing URL in place until Publish runs because the Editorial source still exists and remains editable. Publish no longer checks for missing source, removes source-deleted projections, or reports deletes; DPD-1 has already completed those removals.

Delete Editorial

DPD-1 makes confirmed Editorial Delete immediately remove any exact current public projection and every impacted public inventory. SSP-8 follow-through then removes that exact Editorial child from its Working record. There is no Published-without-Editorial lineage state and no wait for a later Publish.

If the final Editorial child is removed, the record is removed: the still-existing Working document itself is enough to derive the absence of lineage and needs no empty table entry.

Delete Working

Confirmed Working Delete removes its whole lineage record. It does not delete any Editorial child document or public projection. Those artifacts remain useful because the Editorial document is independently editable canonical source; they simply cease to be relevant to tracing a Working document that no longer exists.

An out-of-workflow filesystem deletion performs no lineage mutation. No builder or report scans for missing files to repair the table.

Projects Presentation

Projects remains the complete presentation surface for this Working-owned purpose because every relevant lineage record has a current Working row.

For each Projects document:

  • no Editorial child: no lineage status or icon;
  • one or more Editorial children and no current published_url: Editorial status;
  • any child with a current published_url: Published status.

When several children exist, Published is the highest displayed state. Exact child detail may expose every current Editorial target without inventing a primary child. Projects retains no Folder, Work, or Series subject icon; Project State remains their owner. Analysis retains only its existing publishable: false exclusion icon.

SSP-8 no longer adds a complete orphan-lineage report. Once Working is deleted, the workflow has no lineage question to report. Editorial and public documents continue through their ordinary Analysis and public surfaces.

Delivery Steps

Superseded Review History

  • [x] SSP-8.0 documented the independently nullable-state proposal and report boundary that subsequent review rejected.
  • [x] SSP-8.1 committed the corresponding v2 cutover; it is retained as superseded implementation evidence and is not a base for further mutation work.
  • [x] Complete DPD-1 before resuming SSP-8.

SSP-8.2 — Cut Over To The Working-Owned Table

  • [x] Freeze the smallest exact Working-keyed envelope and zero-to-many Editorial-child representation.
  • [x] Remove lineage_id, nullable Working, independent Published state, empty Working-only records, and v2-only aliases in one clean schema cut.
  • [x] Migrate the current reviewed data explicitly; do not infer rows or state from filesystem availability.
  • [x] Adapt New and exact Replace to the Working-keyed child list without changing Copy UI or response ownership.

SSP-8.2 Evidence

  • The reviewed canonical v2 table contained one dotlineform/projects Working identity with editorial: null. The explicit v3 migration therefore stores the configured dotlineform/projects to analysis/works collection pair and an empty records array; it did not infer an Editorial child or retain an empty Working-only record.
  • The lineage service now parses and writes only the exact v3 envelope. New appends an exact child under the selected Working ID; Replace requires one exact current child and preserves its doc_id, created_at, and published_url while updating last_copied_at.
  • Existing Copy preview/apply ownership and New/Replace decisions remain in the transfer services. The apply receipt remains under lineage and now reports the v3 schema plus record_count; no parallel Copy or lineage mutation surface was added.
  • Existing Publish reconciliation and Projects projection consumers were structurally adapted to the Working-owned table so the clean cut remains loadable. SSP-8.3 still owns Delete mutation and the final published_url follow-through rules; SSP-8.4 still owns presentation correction.
  • Focused verification passed: 75 service, Copy/apply, Publish, and Projects projection tests; explicit Python lint across ten changed Python files; strict v2 rejection and removed-alias checks; repository legacy-contract scan; generated Studio docs/search rebuild; and git diff --check. A bounded final diff review found no parallel lineage owner, compatibility residue, Delete mutation, public payload, or SSP-8.4 presentation change in the checkpoint.

SSP-8.3 — Connect Delete And Publish Follow-Through

  • [ ] After DPD-1 succeeds for an Editorial Delete, remove only that exact child and remove the record when no children remain.
  • [ ] After a Working Delete, remove its complete lineage record without mutating Editorial or public documents.
  • [ ] Keep successful Publish responsible only for published_url on current Editorial children and keep Set Publishable lineage-neutral.
  • [ ] Rebuild only the exact affected private Projects projection and add no scan, repair, rollback, or lineage-specific retry protocol.

SSP-8.4 — Correct Projects Presentation

  • [ ] Show no status/icon for a Working document without Editorial children.
  • [ ] Derive one highest Editorial or Published state across current children while retaining exact zero-to-many detail.
  • [ ] Verify immediate Editorial Delete removes Published presentation, while publishable: false retains Published until the next Publish.
  • [ ] Preserve Analysis exclusion-icon and Project State subject-icon ownership.

SSP-8.5 — Verify And Transfer

  • [ ] Exercise New, Replace, Working Delete, Editorial Delete, Set Publishable, Publish, zero-to-many children, and direct non-lineage documents.
  • [ ] Verify Working-owned table and Projects presentation against the same exact fixtures.
  • [ ] Run focused schema, service, Copy, Delete, Publish, projection, browser, lint, whitespace, generated-data, and public-isolation checks.
  • [ ] Transfer the stable Working-owned lineage contract to durable feature and architecture owners.

Boundaries

SSP-8 does not add content comparison, diff, merge, synchronization, automatic New/Replace choice, identity inference, filesystem polling or reconciliation, unavailable repair, tombstones, event history, a public lineage payload, an orphan-lineage report, or lineage mutation controls. DPD-1 owns immediate public cleanup on document Delete; SSP-8 does not reproduce that machinery.

The delivery is stopped before SSP-8.3 implementation approval. No Delete-lineage mutation or revised Publish behavior has started.
